Which Canadian County offices matter when you sell?

Three offices in El Reno cover almost everything: the Assessor for value, the Treasurer for the bill, and the County Clerk for the deed. The Assessor is at 200 N Choctaw Ave, El Reno, OK 73036. The Treasurer, Jay K. Arnold, is at 314 W. Rogers Street, with a phone of (405) 295-6330, a mailing address of P.O. Box 1095 and hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The county's general line is (405) 295-6000.

The Treasurer's own page describes the job as collecting taxes certified by the Assessor on real estate, personal property and public utilities, then paying them out to the county, cities, towns and schools under levies approved by the Excise Board. It also notes that city special assessments for sewer, water, weeds, cleaning, paving and nuisance abatement are certified to the Treasurer once they turn delinquent, and they sit as a lien on the real estate account.

That last point catches sellers. A mowing or cleanup charge from a town can show up on the county tax account long after the city sent its notice.

What is Canadian County like?

Canadian County is in west-central Oklahoma, covers 905.17 square miles, and sits just west of Oklahoma City, with El Reno as county seat. The Oklahoma Historical Society lists its towns as Calumet, Mustang, Okarche, Piedmont, Union City, Yukon and El Reno. The North Canadian and Canadian rivers cross it from northwest to southeast.

Settlement came through land openings in 1889, 1892 and 1901. Population was 20,110 at 1907 statehood, reached 115,541 in 2010 and was 154,154 in the April 2020 census, which is fast growth for a county that took 63 years to go from statehood to 32,245 residents. Interstate 40 crosses it east to west, and El Reno sits where U.S. Highways 66 and 81 meet, with State Highways 3, 4, 37, 92 and 152 also listed.

With that much growth, houses here range from farmhouses and older railroad-era homes in El Reno to subdivisions built in the last few decades near the Oklahoma City side of the county.

What drives the Canadian County economy?

Agriculture started it, rail built El Reno, and government and schools carry a lot of the jobs today. The Historical Society says El Reno became a rail hub and was the regional headquarters of the Rock Island for about 75 years, with the railroad shut down in 1980. The old yards on the north side of town have stayed mostly vacant since.

The same source gives these employers and anchors:

  • Mustang Public Schools, listed as the county's largest employer at 600 employees at the time of the entry.
  • The Federal Correctional Institution in El Reno, with about 325 workers in the county entry and 430 in the 1990s town entry.
  • The Gary E. Miller Canadian County Children's Justice Center near Banner and the Union City Community Corrections Center.
  • Fort Reno, where the U.S. Department of Agriculture runs a research station.

After World War II, many county residents took civilian jobs at the Federal Aviation Administration's aeronautical center in Oklahoma City and at Tinker Air Force Base in Midwest City. Redlands Community College and the Canadian Valley technology school are also in the El Reno area. For a seller, the pull of Oklahoma City commuting is a bigger story in Yukon, Mustang and Piedmont than in El Reno.

When are Canadian County property taxes due and how do you pay?

Oklahoma bills run on the same cycle statewide: bills go out around November 1, the first half is due by December 31 and the second half before April 1, according to the state's taxpayer pamphlet hosted on the county site. Because the Canadian County Treasurer's page did not list the dates itself, confirm them by phone at (405) 295-6330 before you rely on them.

The Treasurer's tax roll site gives three online payment options and says the processor, not the Treasurer, collects the fees:

  • Debit card: 1.95 percent of the total.
  • Credit card: 2.75 percent of the total.
  • eCheck: $1.50 flat fee.

A returned check carries a $35.00 fee. The state pamphlet adds that unpaid taxes become delinquent after December 31, that interest runs at 1.5 percent per month with no cap, and that a property can end up at a tax sale. It also says each taxing jurisdiction holds a lien on the property that follows it through a change of ownership, so a buyer cannot get clear title until delinquent taxes are paid. That pamphlet is dated 2012, so treat the figures as background and check current rules.

How do you protest a Canadian County valuation?

You file an informal protest on Form OTC 974 within 30 calendar days of the date the change-of-value notice was mailed. The county's protest page said the 2026 notices were expected around April 3, and that owners with no notice could file between April 3 and May 4, 2026.

StepDetail
Informal protestForm OTC 974 with evidence, to 200 N Choctaw Ave, by mail, fax, email or in person
HearingInformal hearing with the Assessor, in person or by phone on request
Assessor decisionFinal action within 7 calendar days of the hearing
Formal appealForm OTC 976 to the Board of Equalization within 15 calendar days of the final-action notice
Further appealCanadian County district court

The Board of Equalization can confirm, correct or adjust a value after taking evidence, and it mails a written decision. The county page lists no deadline for a court appeal, so ask a lawyer promptly if you plan one. Dates and addresses on the page may change from year to year.

What exemptions and freezes exist in Canadian County?

The homestead exemption takes $1,000 off the assessed valuation of your homestead, and the county estimates the savings at $60 to $114 depending on local millage. You must own and live in the property on January 1, and the deed must be signed on or before January 1 and filed with the County Clerk by February 1. New applications are due March 15, and the county said applications went out by mail in January 2026 with a postmark deadline of March 16, 2026.

Two further programs are worth knowing:

  • Additional homestead exemption: another $1,000 for a head of household whose gross household income was $30,000 or less last year.
  • Senior valuation freeze: for owners 65 or older as of January 1 whose prior-year gross household income did not exceed the 2026 limit of $99,000, applied for between January 1 and March 16.

The county stresses that the freeze locks the valuation, not the tax bill, since millage can still change. A separate state refund exists for those 65 or older or totally disabled with income of $12,000 or less, claimed on Form 538-H. When a house sells, the new owner starts the homestead process under their own name, which can mean a higher bill the following year.

What should a Canadian County seller do about taxes before closing?

Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer, check for city special assessments, and confirm who is responsible for the current year. In Oklahoma the owner on January 1 is the one the tax is assessed to, which is why closing agents prorate the bill between buyer and seller.

  1. Call the Treasurer at (405) 295-6330 or look up your parcel on the tax roll site.
  2. Ask whether any city weed, paving, water or nuisance charges have been certified to the county.
  3. Check whether your homestead exemption is on file with the Assessor so the buyer inherits an accurate record.
  4. If the house is behind on taxes, remember the lien runs with the property and clear title needs the delinquent taxes paid.
  5. Keep copies of anything you protested, since the Assessor's final action notice may arrive near closing.

If a house is inherited, vacant or needs repairs, an as-is cash sale can close around a tax balance and skip the repair negotiation. We buy houses in Canadian County, from El Reno to Yukon and Mustang, and the steps above still apply to any sale.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Canadian County Treasurer's office?

The Treasurer is at 314 W. Rogers Street, El Reno, OK 73036, phone (405) 295-6330. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the mailing address is P.O. Box 1095.

How much can the Canadian County Assessor raise my value?

State law caps annual increases in taxable value, but the cap can reset after a sale or after new improvements. Call the Assessor at 200 N Choctaw Ave for your parcel's details.

What is the deadline to protest a Canadian County valuation?

File Form OTC 974 within 30 calendar days of the mailing date of your change-of-value notice. If you got no notice, the county gave a window of April 3 to May 4 for 2026.

What is the Canadian County senior valuation freeze?

It freezes the assessed valuation of a homestead owned by someone 65 or older as of January 1 with prior-year household income at or below the 2026 limit of $99,000. It does not freeze the tax bill.

Can a Canadian County house be sold with delinquent taxes?

Yes, but a lien for unpaid taxes goes with the property, and a buyer cannot get clear title until delinquent taxes are paid. A cash buyer can often pay the balance at closing from proceeds.

Does Canadian County charge to pay property tax online?

The tax roll site lists processor fees of 1.95 percent for debit cards, 2.75 percent for credit cards and $1.50 for an eCheck. Those fees go to the payment company, not the Treasurer.

Where is Tulsa County and what does it cover?

Tulsa County is in northeast Oklahoma, with Tulsa as its county seat and largest city. It was created at statehood in 1907 and is the second most populous county in Oklahoma, behind Oklahoma County.

The county covers 587 square miles, of which 570 are land. The Arkansas River drains most of it, Keystone Lake lies partly inside it, and Bird Creek and the Caney River drain the north. The Census Bureau counted 669,279 people in 2020, and the 2025 estimate shown on Wikipedia is 698,782. It borders Washington, Rogers, Wagoner, Okmulgee, Creek, Pawnee and Osage counties.

Several cities sit wholly or partly inside it: Bixby, Broken Arrow, Collinsville, Glenpool, Jenks, Owasso, Sand Springs, Sapulpa, Skiatook and Tulsa, plus the towns of Liberty, Lotsee and Sperry. Which city a house is in affects its permits and school boundaries, so name the city when you ask a county office about an address.

What are the main numbers behind Tulsa County property?

The county budget and census figures below give a sense of scale. They come from the county clerk's budget document and the 2020 census.

ItemFigure
Assessed valuation, January 2025$8,265,978,832
Homestead exemption amount added back in the budget$107,153,180
Housing units, 2020 census292,375
Vacant share of housing units, 20208.7%
Owner-occupied share of occupied homes, 202057.9%

Typical June tax auction size475 to 500 properties

About 42% of occupied homes are rented, so many Tulsa County properties are rentals. The assessor values property as of January 1, so landlords should check whose name the assessor shows for that date.

How does the Tulsa County Assessor value a home?

The assessor sets a Fair Cash (Market) Value as of January 1 each year, using market sales from the 24 months before that date. The office says it weighs location, size, quality of construction, condition and age, and it revalues residential property in Tulsa County every year.

Three numbers appear on a notice. Fair Cash Value is the market estimate. Taxable Fair Cash Value is the figure the tax is based on, and it cannot rise more than 3% a year with a homestead exemption or agricultural use, or 5% for other real property, unless title transfers or improvements are added. The Assessed Value (Gross) is currently 11% of the taxable figure (Tulsa County Assessor FAQ).

The cap matters at sale time. The assessor states that the cap on taxable value is removed when a property is purchased, which is why a buyer's first tax bill can be higher than the seller's. A seller who has owned for many years may have a lower taxable value than the market value suggests.

How can I protest a Tulsa County valuation?

Start with an informal protest at the assessor's office. If you disagree with the outcome you can file a formal appeal with the Board of Equalization, and further appeals go to District Court.

  • Only the owner of record on January 1, or a designated representative with written authorization, can protest the current year value.
  • You have 30 calendar days from the date on the Notice of Valuation, or you can file on or before the first Monday in April if the value did not change.
  • Forms go by mail, in person, or by email to informalprotest@tulsacounty.org, and hearings can be held by phone.
  • Photos, independent appraisals and repair estimates help. Sales after January 1 of the current year are not considered.

The assessor's staff also say that notices are mailed only when the market or taxable value increases. If you did not get one, your value stayed the same or went down. Storm, flood or fire damage should be reported to the assessor at 918-596-5100 with any insurance or fire marshal report.

Which Tulsa County exemptions apply to a homeowner?

The Tulsa County Assessor lists six kinds of relief: the homestead exemption, the additional homestead exemption, the senior valuation limitation, the circuit breaker refund, the 100% disabled veteran exemption and religious or charitable exemptions.

  • Homestead: $1,000 off the assessed valuation of a primary residence. The application is due by March 15, or within 30 days of the valuation notice date, to count for that year.
  • Additional homestead: another $1,000 for homestead owners with gross household income of $30,000 or less (effective January 1, 2024). Owners under 65 must file each year.
  • Senior valuation limitation: freezes taxable value for owners 65 and older who qualify for homestead and fall under the HUD income limit.
  • Circuit breaker (538-H): a refund for qualifying low-income owners, capped at $200, with claims due to the Oklahoma Tax Commission by June 30.

Owners file these applications with the assessor's Taxpayer Services office on the 5th floor of the county headquarters, 218 W. Sixth Street, or online.

Who collects property tax in Tulsa County, and how do payments work?

The Tulsa County Treasurer collects the tax at 218 W. 6th Street, 8th Floor, in Tulsa. Payments can be made in person, by mail, by phone or online through the county's tax roll site.

Online fees are charged by the payment processor, not the county: 2.35% for credit cards with a $1.95 minimum, 1.95% for debit cards, and $1.75 for an electronic check up to $100,000. The Treasurer's home page warns taxpayers that Doxo.com is not affiliated with the office and should not be used for property tax. Statements go out in November, with remote bank collection sites open for three weeks after Thanksgiving (Tulsa County Treasurer).

Tulsa County does not prorate tax at sale. If tax is outstanding, the title company can collect part from the seller and part from the buyer and send it in. If the year's tax is not yet certified and nothing is owed, the buyer usually receives a credit at closing for the seller's share and then pays the full bill (Treasurer FAQ).

What happens when Tulsa County taxes go unpaid?

Unpaid taxes can lead to the June real estate auction. The Treasurer holds it on the second Monday of June, and the 2027 date is June 14, 2027. In an average year the county auctions 475 to 500 properties for unpaid taxes or special assessments such as cleaning and mowing.

MonthTreasurer mailing or action
NovemberOriginal tax statements, with a second resale notice if a property is scheduled for auction
JanuaryNew owner and first delinquent statements
MarchFinal notification of tax resale
MayResale publication and land list
JuneJune resale auction
JulyUnsold properties move to the Commissioners' sale list

A statute change effective November 1, 2025 requires payment before the start of the auction to remove a property from it, and the Treasurer gives 5:00 p.m. on June 11, 2027 as the cutoff. Properties that do not sell become county property that can be bought through the Commissioners' sale process (Treasurer calendar).

An owner who is 65 or older or totally disabled, lives in a single-family home that is not a rental, has gross income below the Federal Poverty Guidelines, and has an assessor value of $180,000 or less may qualify for an exemption from tax resale. The application must be filed before the resale each year.

What should Tulsa County sellers check about title and records?

Deeds and death certificates are recorded with the Tulsa County Clerk, and the assessor updates its records from what the clerk receives. If the assessor's site shows the wrong owner, the usual causes are an unrecorded deed, an error on a recorded deed, or a lot split that will not show until the next year's roll.

  • A surviving joint tenant on a deed with a right of survivorship clause can file an affidavit with a certified death certificate. Without that clause, the assessor advises talking to an attorney.
  • To split or combine lots inside Tulsa or the unincorporated county, call INCOG at 918-584-7526. Other cities have their own planning offices.
  • A manufactured home sale or move needs an OTC 936 form from the assessor.
  • A parcel is taxed as it existed on January 1, so a lot you sold in part after that date still produces a bill for the whole parcel.

Clear these before listing. A cash buyer can often work through title problems, but each one adds time at the title company.

How does a cash sale handle Tulsa County tax due?

The title company pays unpaid property tax from the sale proceeds, so the tax does not have to be paid before you accept an offer.

Frequently asked questions

When are Tulsa County property taxes due?

At least half must be paid before January 1, and the second half before April 1. Taxes of $25 or less must be paid in full before January 1. Late payments are subject to interest, costs and fees.

Does Tulsa County prorate taxes when a house sells?

No. The county bills the full year, and the closing company usually divides it between buyer and seller on the closing statement.

How do I protest my Tulsa County value?

File an informal protest with the Assessor within 30 calendar days of the valuation notice, or by the first Monday in April if your value did not change. Call 918-596-5100 or email informalprotest@tulsacounty.org.

What is the Tulsa County tax auction date for 2027?

The Treasurer lists June 14, 2027, the second Monday of June. Payment to remove a property must be made before the auction starts, with a 5:00 p.m. cutoff on June 11, 2027.

When do I file for the homestead exemption?

Applications are accepted all year, but to count for the current year they must be filed by March 15 or within 30 days of the date on the valuation notice. Later filings take effect the following year.

Where is McClain County and what does it cover?

McClain County sits in south central Oklahoma and belongs to the Oklahoma City metropolitan area. Its county seat is Purcell. The county covers about 580 square miles, nearly all of it land, and is bordered by Cleveland, Pottawatomie, Pontotoc, Garvin and Grady counties.

The South Canadian River forms the northern edge. The western half is hilly with blackjack oak, while the eastern half is level lowland. For a seller, that split matters mostly for yard drainage and for how far a house sits from the interstate, not for anything exotic.

The cities are Blanchard, Newcastle and Purcell. Towns include Byars, Cole, Dibble, Goldsby, Maysville, Rosedale, Washington and Wayne. Criner, Payne and Woody Chapel are unincorporated. Your property tax bill depends partly on which of these, and which school district, your parcel falls in.

How did McClain County get its shape?

Railroads built most of the towns. The Southern Kansas line came south and a Texas line came north in the late 1880s, and they met at what became Purcell. Later lines founded Washington, Cole and Blanchard.

Purcell was a starting point for the Land Run of 1889 and sat on the boundary between Indian Territory and Oklahoma Territory. The county was part of the Chickasaw Nation until statehood. The county was named for Charles M. McClain, who attended the state constitutional convention.

The railroad towns and the interstate corridor are where most parcels and most tax bills are concentrated.

What is the economy like for homeowners in McClain County?

The county economy began with farming and cattle, and many residents now commute to the Oklahoma City area. Early in the 1900s each town had a cotton gin and Purcell had a flour mill. Mid-America Area Vo-Tech opened in 1971, and the Chickasaw Nation runs a casino at Newcastle.

The 2020 Census counted 41,662 residents, 16,421 housing units and 79.8 percent owner occupancy. About 7.2 percent of units were vacant. The median age was 39.2 and 26.1 percent of residents were under 18, which points to a family-heavy owner base.

Which roads and school districts matter when selling a McClain County house?

Interstate 35 is the busiest road. It enters at Goldsby over the McCall Bridge, runs beside the Canadian River through Purcell and exits toward Garvin County. Interstate 44 crosses the northwest, and the H.E. Bailey Turnpike Norman Spur links it to US 62, US 277 and State Highway 9 south of Newcastle.

Buyers ask about commute and schools first. The county lists these full K-12 districts:

  • Alex, Asher, Blanchard, Bridge Creek and Dibble
  • Lindsay, Maysville, Newcastle, Norman and Paoli
  • Purcell, Stratford, Washington and Wayne

Because school districts levy their own taxes, two houses of equal value in different districts can carry different bills.

Who handles property tax in McClain County?

Two elected offices split the work. The County Assessor, Elizabeth Patrick, values property and prepares the tax roll. The County Treasurer, Michelle Williams, collects the money and hands it to the county, cities, towns and schools.

OfficeDetails

The assessor sends values to the County Equalization Board and then the State Board of Equalization. After the Excise Board certifies millage rates, the assessor builds the roll and gives it to the treasurer. See the McClain County Assessor page and the treasurer page.

What do McClain County sellers usually face?

The common situations are inherited homes, houses with deferred repairs, rentals with tenants in place and parcels with back taxes. Roughly one in five occupied homes here is rented, based on the 2020 Census.

A fast cash sale suits owners who want to skip showings, inspection negotiations and a lender's repair list. Whatever route you take, get a written payoff of taxes and any city liens before choosing, so the net figure is clear.

How is a McClain County tax bill built from the assessment?

The assessor sets values, the Excise Board certifies millage, and the treasurer bills the result. One mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of taxable value, and the Oklahoma Policy Institute says assessment ratios run between 10 and 15 percent and mill rates commonly fall between 90 and 110.

Every local government sets its own levy, and each property's total rate combines county, city or town and school district levies. A house in Newcastle and one in Wayne can sit in different school districts and so see different bills.

  • Value comes from the assessor, who inspects each real property on a four-year cycle.
  • Levies come from the taxing bodies and are certified by the Excise Board.
  • The bill goes out from the treasurer once the roll is filed.

The first installment is not delinquent until 30 days after the assessor files the completed rolls with the treasurer, according to the statute.

When is McClain County property tax due and what happens if it is late?

Oklahoma law makes ad valorem tax payable on November 1, and McClain County follows the statewide schedule. If at least half is not paid before January 1, the whole levy turns delinquent. If half is paid, the rest is due before April 1.

  • Balances of $25 or less must be paid in full before January 1.
  • Delinquent tax accrues 1.5 percent interest per month, capped at the unpaid tax amount.
  • Mortgage servicers pay one annual payment before January 1.
  • The treasurer may waive penalty or interest incurred through no fault of the taxpayer.

Sellers who close between November and March should find out whether the first half has been paid, because the treasurer will not take a second-half payment on a delinquent account the same way.

How do you contest a McClain County valuation?

Start with a written protest to the assessor. After a notice of increased valuation, you have 30 calendar days from the mailing date. For unchanged values, the protest is due by the first Monday in April.

The assessor holds an informal hearing and must send a written decision within 7 calendar days. If you disagree, you have 15 calendar days from the mailing date of that decision to appeal to the county board of equalization. The protest form should be filed with the required valuation information, or the assessor's number is presumed correct on appeal.

Oklahoma also caps annual growth in the assessed value of a primary home at 3 percent unless it sells, and the homestead exemption removes $1,000 from taxable value, according to the Oklahoma Policy Institute overview. A sale can reset that cap, so a buyer's first bill can look higher than yours.

What does selling a house with tax due look like in McClain County?

Unpaid property tax is settled out of sale proceeds at closing, so the title company asks the treasurer for a payoff. City charges for weeds, cleanup, paving or nuisance abatement are certified to the treasurer once delinquent and sit as a lien on the parcel.

The treasurer also manages county-owned property acquired at annual delinquent-tax sales, so a parcel left unpaid for long enough can leave the owner's hands. If you are behind, inherited a house with back taxes, or need to sell quickly, a direct conversation about the real payoff number is the fastest way to know your options.

Rural parcels near the Canadian and Washita rivers, hilly lots in the west, and older homes in Purcell and Byars each present different repair questions. Selling as-is to a cash buyer removes the need to fix them first.

Where is Grady County, Oklahoma, and how is it laid out?

Grady County lies in south-central Oklahoma and covers 1,105.30 square miles, with Chickasha as the county seat. The Oklahoma Historical Society places Canadian County to the north, McClain and Garvin to the east, Stephens to the south, and Caddo and Comanche to the west.

Those rivers and their creeks drain the county, which is why farm and pasture acreage has always been a big part of Grady County tax rolls.

Eleven towns besides Chickasha were incorporated at the time of the 2010 census: Alex, Amber, Bradley, Bridge Creek, Minco, Ninnekah, Norge, Pocasset, Rush Springs, Tuttle and Verden. The same treasurer bills homes in all of them.

Where is Muskogee County and who lives there?

Fort Gibson was founded on the Grand River in 1824, and the town beside it claims to be the oldest in Oklahoma. The Katy railroad reached the area after the Civil War, and the depot named Muscogee grew into the city. The post office changed the spelling to Muskogee in 1900.

In 1874 the federal government consolidated the Five Civilized Tribes agencies into one Union Agency near Muscogee, a federal court opened there in 1889, and the Dawes Commission set up headquarters in 1894. Agriculture came first, then food processing, sand and gravel, brick and glass. State and federal jobs have long mattered, especially education and veterans' services, along with light manufacturing, health care and social services. The town of Taft hosts two state prisons.

The McClellan-Kerr Arkansas River Navigation System, dedicated in 1971, opened year-round commercial traffic and led to the Port of Muskogee. Education has deep roots here too, from Bacone College, which moved to the area in 1885, to a Northeastern State University branch that opened in 1994.

The county contains 12 cities and 8 towns, according to the Wikipedia county article. The list matters for sellers because the city and school district shape the levies on a tax bill.

Three interstates cross the county core: I-35, I-40 and I-44. The county article also lists I-235, I-240, I-335 and I-344, US 62, US 77, US 270, and the Turner, Kilpatrick and Kickapoo turnpikes.

Homes near that corridor will sit differently with buyers than homes on a quiet side street in Warr Acres or The Village.

Transit is thinner. The city's bus system, Embark, uses a hub-and-spoke layout with limited coverage of the main street grid, and a streetcar loop of 6.9 miles serves Bricktown, Midtown and Downtown. Outside those areas, most buyers assume a car.

Hail and wind are the main roof risks. Oklahoma City has a humid subtropical climate, and Wikipedia says the city is prone to severe hail, especially in a March to June storm season.

Applications run from January 1 to March 15, or 30 days after a valuation notice if that is later. If you change the deed or move, the Assessor says you need to refile, so a seller should expect the exemption to end with the sale and a buyer should apply fresh.

The Cimarron River forms part of the northern boundary, the North Canadian River crosses the county from northwest to southeast, and Fort Supply Lake sits on Wolf Creek. With about 16 people per square mile in 2010, this is open country. A house on acreage, a farmhouse or a town lot in Woodward, Mooreland or Fort Supply can each have different tax and access questions, so say which one you own when you call a county office.

Woodward County was created in September 1893 as County N when the Cherokee Outlet opened to settlement, and residents chose the Woodward name in an election on November 6, 1894.

The ground was already a military crossroads. Camp Supply was set up in November 1868 as a depot, later becoming Fort Supply, and Texas cattle moved through the southwest corner on the Great Western Trail from 1876 into the 1880s. Wind turbines seven miles north of Woodward began commercial production in 2003, and CF Industries runs an ammonia facility. Beaver Express Service is headquartered in Woodward.

What is Cleveland County, Oklahoma, like?

Cleveland County is a 558.34-square-mile county in central Oklahoma, south of Oklahoma County and north of the Canadian River, with Norman as county seat. Its neighbors are Oklahoma County to the north, Pottawatomie County to the east, McClain County to the south and Canadian County to the west. It was organized after the Organic Act of May 2, 1890 as County Three, and voters picked the name Cleveland over Lincoln in an August 1890 election. The Land Run of 1889 opened the Unassigned Lands on April 22, and towns such as Norman, Moore and Noble grew up along the railroad. Who handles property tax in Beckham County?

Two county offices in Sayre split the work: the Assessor sets values and the Treasurer collects the bill. The Treasurer, Jennifer Drury, can be reached at (580) 928-2589 or Treasurer@beckhamcountyok.gov, with mail going to P.O. Box 600, Sayre, OK 73662.

The Assessor's own site is blunt about its limits. It says the office does not set tax rates, adopt budgets or collect taxes. Those rates come from the local taxing jurisdictions, and the assessor's page offers a property tax estimator and school district mill rate lookup. The Treasurer's page adds that the Treasurer collects and apportions all ad valorem taxes for the county and its subdivisions and enforces collection of delinquent taxes through tax sales.

If your question is "why is my value what it is," call the Assessor. If it is "how much do I owe and when," call the Treasurer.

When is Beckham County property tax due?

Taxes become due on November 1, and you can pay the full amount or the first half by December 31. The second half is due by March 31. The Treasurer says statements of $25 or less must be paid in full.

DateWhat happens in Beckham County
March 15Assessor deadline for homestead and other exemptions and for personal property renditions without penalty
October 1Assessor certifies the tax amounts to be collected

Penalty starts at 1.5 percent per month after December 31, and the second half starts accruing in April. A missing statement does not excuse the tax; the Treasurer cites O.S. 68 section 2915 for that. If a mortgage company escrows your taxes, the statement goes to the lender instead of you, and the Treasurer notes that lender payments often arrive at the end of December and may not post until early January.

Online payment is available at the Treasurer's tax roll page. The posted third-party charges are $1.75 for an eCheck and 2.95 percent of the tax for a card, and there is a drop box at the security desk in the courthouse lobby. The site said at the time we read it that its online tax information covers tax years 2018 through 2024, so ask the office for anything outside that window.

How does the Beckham County Assessor value a house?

The Assessor estimates market value with recognized appraisal methods and applies the state's assessment ratio to get assessed value. Exemptions come off after that, leaving taxable value, which is the figure the millage rates are applied to.

The office lists the factors it looks at:

  • Recent sales and market activity in the area.
  • Size, age, quality and condition of the house.
  • Location and neighborhood influences.
  • Construction type, additions and new building.
  • Comparable properties.

State law caps how much taxable market value can rise in a year. The Assessor's page gives 3 percent for agricultural property or residential property with a homestead exemption and 5 percent for other property. Its example is a $200,000 value, which could rise to $206,000 with a homestead or $210,000 without. The page also says the cap resets if the property is sold or transferred, so a buyer may see a value jump the year after a sale even when the seller's bill grew slowly.

How do you protest a Beckham County valuation?

The Tax Commission's form says that missing the 30 days makes the assessor's value final for that year. The assessor must then hold an informal hearing, and the form lists a phone option and an in-person option. A taxpayer who is still unhappy can appeal to the county board of equalization on Form 976, and the form notes that all protest proceedings must be completed by May 31 or the board's adjournment date.

The Assessor's site suggests bringing photographs, measurements, sales information or correction details. For a seller, an appeal is rarely worth chasing right before closing, but a value error that persists will follow the buyer.

What exemptions apply to a Beckham County home?

The main one is the homestead exemption, which takes $1,000 off the assessed valuation of your primary residence. To qualify you must be an Oklahoma resident who lives in the home by January 1. The Assessor's page gave a due date of March 15, 2026 for that tax year, and applications can be made at the office or by mailing Form OTC 921.

You do not have to renew while you still live there and the deed has not changed. That last clause matters when you sell, because a new owner has to apply under their own name. The Assessor also holds in-person sessions for exemptions and personal property, and the site flagged an upcoming schedule when we visited.

What is Beckham County like for a home seller?

Beckham County is in southwestern Oklahoma, formed at 1907 statehood and covering 904.14 square miles, with Sayre as county seat. The Oklahoma Historical Society reports that the county's economy has been based principally on agriculture and livestock, with wheat, cotton and alfalfa among the crops. It also notes an oil boom and bust in the late 1970s and early 1980s, and that Elk City's first producing Shell well came in on November 24, 1947.

The incorporated towns are Carter, Elk City, Erick, Sayre, Sweetwater and Texola. Elk City sits at Interstate 40 and State Highway 6 and is 18 miles northeast of Sayre. The 2020 census counted 22,411 people in the county and 11,566 in Elk City. Sayre's courthouse, finished in 1911 and dedicated in 1912, is on the National Register of Historic Places. The Elk City area also has the National Route 66 Museum within its Old Town Museum Complex.

Interstate 40, U.S. Highway 283 and several state highways serve the county, and municipal airports exist in Elk City and Erick. Because the county is mostly small towns and farmland, many sellers hold older houses, rural parcels or inherited property, and the tax calendar above affects all of them.

What taxes and fees show up when a Beckham County house changes hands?

The deed itself carries documentary stamp tax, and Oklahoma's Tax Commission notice sets it at $0.75 per $500 of consideration, excluding liens left on the property, on deeds worth more than $100. Stamps are bought when the deed is offered to the county clerk, and the buyer's complete address must be on the face of the deed. A seller claiming an exemption must write the statute reference on the deed, and the older note about consideration under $100 no longer suffices. Confirm the current rate with the clerk, since the notice we read is dated 1999.

The Treasurer's mortgage tax is separate and applies to mortgages, not to ordinary deeds. It runs from 2 cents to 10 cents per $100 depending on the term, plus a $10.00 certification fee per mortgage. If the buyer is using cash, no mortgage tax comes into play.

Delinquent property can be sold at the June resale once the county has held a tax lien for two full years, according to the Treasurer. Taxes owed are usually settled from sale proceeds at closing, so ask the Treasurer for a current balance before you sign. A cash buyer can close around a tax balance, which helps when the house is behind.

Frequently asked questions

When are Beckham County property taxes due?

Where is McCurtain County and how big is it?

McCurtain County fills the southeastern corner of Oklahoma. At 1,902 square miles it is the third-largest county in the state, and the county seat is Idabel. The 2020 Census counted 30,814 residents, spread across a lot of ground.

The north rises into the foothills of the Ouachita Mountains. The south drops to the Red River bottoms, and the lowest point in Oklahoma is on the Little River where it leaves the state for Arkansas. Broken Bow Lake was created in 1968 by damming the Mountain Fork River.

Agriculture and forestry led the economy. The original forests were cleared within two decades of statehood, cotton gave way to cattle, swine and poultry, and reforestation has made timber important again. Limestone, sand and gravel are mined for local use.

Where is Craig County, Oklahoma, and what does it include?

Craig County sits in the northeast corner of Oklahoma, with Kansas along its northern edge. It covers 762.71 square miles, and Vinita is the county seat, according to the Oklahoma Historical Society encyclopedia.

Five incorporated towns sit inside the county lines: Bluejacket, Big Cabin, Ketchum, Vinita and Welch. Smaller places such as White Oak, Wimer and Hudson are unincorporated or have faded. A house in any of these places is billed by the same county treasurer, even though the city or school levy on the bill differs.

The land is mostly rolling prairie, with sandstone hills and long mounds in the west and a rougher stretch called the Neosho Lowlands in the east and south. Big Cabin Creek drains the southern part. For a seller, that mix means a Craig County parcel can be a town lot, a few acres of pasture or a hay field, and the tax paperwork for each can look quite different.

How did Craig County come to be?

The state constitutional convention created Craig County, naming it for Granville Craig, a Cherokee farmer who lived near Welch and Bluejacket from 1873. Before that, the area belonged to the Delaware and Cooweescoowee districts of the Cherokee Nation.

Two railroads shaped the map. The Missouri, Kansas and Texas line ran north to south in 1871, and the Atlantic and Pacific line came east to west the same year. Vinita grew where they crossed. The Vinita entry notes that the town was incorporated under a Cherokee Council law, and that it became the governmental center when the county was formed in 1907.

  • 1871: two rail lines reach the area.
  • 1907: statehood, with Vinita as the seat.
  • 1935: the Grand River Dam Authority begins the Pensacola Dam, which forms Grand Lake O' the Cherokees.
  • 2020: the census counted 14,104 residents in the county.

The county population peaked near 21,000 around 1940 and has stayed between roughly 14,000 and 15,000 since 1980.

What drives the Craig County economy?

Farming, ranching, energy and public employers have carried Craig County for a century. The state encyclopedia lists hay, soybeans, wheat, sorghum and corn as the main crops, and says many ranches remain active in the western half of the county.

Coal was mined by underground and surface methods after the Civil War, and an oil refinery operated west of Vinita as early as 1911. The 1940 completion of Pensacola Dam brought the Grand River Dam Authority, Northeast Oklahoma Electric Cooperative and KAMO Electric into the local economy, and the Vinita encyclopedia says the co-ops still keep significant operations in town.

Government work has also mattered. Eastern State Hospital opened in 1912 on the northeast edge of Vinita and was one of the county's largest employers until operations shrank in the late 1990s. A state corrections facility later took over part of that land.

You protest first with the county assessor, in writing, within 30 calendar days of the date the valuation notice was mailed. The Oklahoma Tax Commission's Form 974 spells out the process under 68 O.S. 2876.

  3. Attend the informal hearing, which can be held by phone if you ask.
  4. Wait for the assessor's written decision, due within seven calendar days of the hearing.

If the assessor did not change your value from the year before, the form allows a protest up to the first Monday in April. The form also says proceedings must wrap up by May 31 or the board's adjournment date. Miss the 30-day window and the proposed value becomes final for that tax year.

Yes. City and town charges such as weed cutting, cleanup, paving and nuisance abatement are sent to the county treasurer once they are delinquent, and they become a lien on the property account.

Call the Craig County Treasurer at 918-256-2286 for bills and payments. The office is at 210 W. Delaware, Suite 104 in Vinita and is open weekdays from 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM. Valuation questions go to the county assessor at the courthouse.

What is the deadline to protest a Craig County valuation?

You have 30 calendar days from the date the valuation notice was mailed to file a written protest with the assessor. If your value did not change from last year, the form allows a protest until the first Monday in April.

Does Craig County list a late fee on its treasurer site?

State law makes the whole levy delinquent on January 1 unless half has been paid before then, and the remainder is due before April 1.

Can I sell a Craig County house with taxes still owed?

Yes. The balance is normally paid from your sale proceeds at closing. Ask the treasurer for a written total and clear any city special assessments that were certified to the county.
